root_cause.text: XLAT's BPF protocol translation helpers only translate the header of the head skb but not the skbs in the frag_list, causing skb_segment_list to process partially translated GRO packets with protocol inconsistencies.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states "XLAT only translates the header of the head skb. Consequently, skbs in the frag_list may remain untranslated, resulting in protocol inconsistencies and reduced throughput." The patch fixes this by setting SKB_GSO_DODGY flag in bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6 and bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4 functions (net/core/filter.c), and then checking for this flag in the GSO segmentation functions (tcp_offload.c, udp_offload.c, tcpv6_offload.c) to prevent skb_segment_list from being called on these partially translated packets, forcing them to use the safer skb_segment path instead.

net: gso: fix tcp fraglist segmentation after pull from frag_list

Detect tcp gso fraglist skbs with corrupted geometry
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 17bd3bd82f9f79f3feba15476c2b2c95a9b11ff8
Author: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>
Date:   Thu Sep 26 10:53:14 2024 +0200

    net: gso: fix tcp fraglist segmentation after pull from frag_list
    
    Detect tcp gso fraglist skbs with corrupted geometry (see below) and
    pass these to skb_segment instead of skb_segment_list, as the first
    can segment them correctly.
    
    Valid SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST skbs
    - consist of two or more segments
    - the head_skb holds the protocol headers pl
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces a fix that detects corrupted SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST geometry. The vulnerable code path was calling __tcp4_gso_segment_list() unconditionally for all SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST packets. The fix adds a validation check: `if (skb_pagelen(skb) - th->doff * 4 == skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_size)` which verifies that the head_skb size matches the expected gso_size. Only if this condition is true does it proceed to __tcp4_gso_segment_list(). If the geometry is corrupted (e.g., due to BPF pull operations that break the invariants), it falls through to regular skb_segment processing by setting `skb->ip_summed = CHECKSUM_NONE`. This prevents the NULL pointer dereference in __tcpv4_gso_segment_list_csum that occurred when processing partially translated or corrupted frag_list packets. The vulnerable construct (unconditional call to __tcp4_gso_segment_list for all SKB_GSO_FRAGLIST packets) is not present in this version - it has been replaced with the protective check.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
bpf: fix bpf_skb_adjust_net/bpf_skb_proto_xlat to deal with gso sctp skbs

SCTP GSO skbs have a gso_size of GSO_BY_FRAGS
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d02f51cbcf12b09ab945873e35046045875eed9a
Author: Daniel Axtens <dja@axtens.net>
Date:   Sat Mar 3 03:03:46 2018 +0100

    bpf: fix bpf_skb_adjust_net/bpf_skb_proto_xlat to deal with gso sctp skbs
    
    SCTP GSO skbs have a gso_size of GSO_BY_FRAGS, so any sort of
    unconditionally mangling of that will result in nonsense value
    and would corrupt the skb later on.
    
    Therefore, i) add two helpers skb_increase_gso_size() and
    skb_decrease_gso_size() that would throw a one
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces fixes for the vulnerability described in the root cause. The diff shows that all four affected functions (bpf_skb_proto_4_to_6, bpf_skb_proto_6_to_4, bpf_skb_net_grow, bpf_skb_net_shrink) now include early checks: 'if (skb_is_gso(skb) && unlikely(skb_is_gso_sctp(skb))) return -ENOTSUPP;' at lines 2090-2091, 2132-2133, 2258-2259, and 2288-2289 respectively. These checks prevent the functions from processing SCTP GSO skbs that use GSO_BY_FRAGS, which would otherwise cause corruption. Additionally, the direct gso_size manipulations are replaced with safer helper functions (skb_decrease_gso_size and skb_increase_gso_size) that include their own validation. The vulnerable construct (unconditional gso_size manipulation on SCTP GSO packets) is now guarded by proper checks, making this a bug-fixing commit rather than a bug-introducing one.
